SOURCE EXTRACT — read from the full djvu text, 2026-09-06
=========================================================
YMCA YEAR BOOK AND OFFICIAL ROSTERS (1921)
New York: Association Press. Internet Archive: ymcayearbookoffi00youn

NOT LENDING-RESTRICTED. The complete djvu text (1,826,321 bytes) was downloaded and searched.

THIS SERIES WAS UNKNOWN TO THIS PROJECT BEFORE 2026-09-06. It is an ANNUAL North American roster of
every YMCA association, branch by branch, with every paid officer named and titled — plus an
alphabetical index of employed officers giving each man's post AND HIS YEAR OF ENTRY INTO
ASSOCIATION WORK. It was found by running "Harold C. Cross" in the p_430 name sweep.

FIRST, THE NULL, BECAUSE IT MATTERS FOR HOW THE SERIES IS USED:
  "Kanawana" occurs ZERO times in the volume.
  "summer camp" and "boys' camp" occur ZERO times.
  The Quebec section contains the word "camp" ZERO times.
THIS IS A ROSTER OF ASSOCIATIONS AND THEIR STAFF, NOT OF THEIR PROGRAMMES. It will never name the
camp. What it names is THE MEN, with their posts and their start dates, which is precisely what this
project lacks for the camp's first forty years.


===============================================================================

WHAT IS IN THAT LIST FOR KANAWANA:

  **Industrial, John G. MacKinnon** — the camp's leader in 1916, 1917, part of 1918 and 1919. THE
  FULL FIRST NAME IS NEW, and it probably resolves a split in `directors-index.md`, which carries
  "John McKinnon, Boys' Work Secretary at Central" for the 1915 split season and "J. G. MacKinnon"
  for 1916-19 as if they might be two men. The index below gives his entry into Association work as
  1915, which is exactly when "John McKinnon" appears. Same man, on this evidence, with the 1915
  annual report spelling the surname Mc.

  **Community, Grant D. Brandon** — the camp's director in 1921 and its relief director for a
  fortnight in August 1918. THE FULL FIRST NAME IS NEW: this project had only "G. D. Brandon".

  **Asst. Physical, Hay Finlay** (Central Branch) — the camp's Senior Section Director in 1922. Note
  the title carefully: the 1922 brochure calls him "ex-Central YMCA Boys' Physical Director", and the
  1921 roster has him as ASSISTANT PHYSICAL at Central, with the Boys' secretary at Central being
  R. E. G. Davis. The brochure's phrasing is looser than the roster's. RECORDED, NOT RECONCILED.
  Note also that "Hay" is printed as a given name in an alphabetical list of surnames — so it is his
  name and not an initial, which the name sweep could not settle from the camp's own paper.

  **Consulting, D. A. Budge** — the general secretary of the founding era, still on the staff in
  1921 in a consulting role, forty-seven years after entering Association work (see the index).

  **President, A. O. Dawson** — noted only because `people/ralph-dawson.md` cannot identify Ralph H.
  Dawson. A. O. Dawson is a DIFFERENT man and no connection is claimed; the name is recorded so that
  a later pass does not mistake one for the other.

AND THE ADDRESS: **127 Drummond St.** in 1921, for the association and for the Central Branch. Every
later directory this project holds gives 1441 Drummond. The move is undated here.


===============================================================================
2. THE ALPHABETICAL LIST OF EMPLOYED OFFICERS
===============================================================================
Its own header and legend, printed at the top of the list:

    "ALPHABETICAL LIST OF EMPLOYED OFFICERS
     June 1, 1921
     The figures after each name indicate THE YEAR OF ENTRY INTO ASSOCIATION WORK"

The entries for men this project has reason to care about, quoted exactly:

    Cross, H. C., Victoria, B. C., Boys', 12
    Brandon, G. D., Montreal, Que., Community, 13
    Finlay, Hay, Montreal, Que., Central, Asst. Physical, 14
    MacKinnon, J. G., Montreal, Que., Industrial, 15
    McEwen, N. F., St. John, N. B., Boys', 18
    Budge, D. A., Montreal, Que., Consulting, 74

**HAROLD C. CROSS IS THE BIG ONE.** `harold-cross.md` says he was "based at the Victoria, British
Columbia YMCA from 1919 to 1925 (role unspecified; LIKELY Boys' Work Secretary or similar)". The
1921 roster prints, under BRITISH COLUMBIA / Victoria: "Physical, W. S. Maguire — **Boys, Harold C.
Cross**". So the role is no longer "likely". And the index's "12" pushes his entry into YMCA employed
work back to **1912**, seven years before the Victoria period this project dates from — which opens a
question that did not exist yesterday: **where was he between 1912 and 1919?**

Others: NELSON F. McEWEN gains a middle initial and a start — Saint John, New Brunswick, Boys' Work,
entered 1918 — a quarter-century before the national boys' work secretaryship this project holds him
in. D. A. BUDGE entered Association work in **1874**.

NOT IN THE 1921 LIST AT ALL: Spinney, Powter, Ereaux, Charlton, Owens. That is not a null about the
men; the list is of PAID OFFICERS, and Spinney was a schoolmaster and Powter a schoolmaster with his
own camp. It is consistent with what f_4958 and f_4960 established — the camp's educational and
section staff were volunteers and seasonal employees drawn from the schools, not association
secretaries.


===============================================================================
3. WHAT THE SERIES IS WORTH — the reason this file exists
===============================================================================
This is ONE YEAR of an annual series. Every volume gives, for every association in the United States
and Canada: the complete named staff by branch, and an index of every employed officer with his post
and his year of entry. For a project whose hardest problem is that its camp directors are initials on
a brochure, that is the single most useful reference series found so far — better than the camping
literature, because the camping literature starts in 1936 and this does not.

The obvious next step is to enumerate the other volumes on the Internet Archive and sweep the
Montreal roster year by year from the 1890s to the 1950s. Tracked as p_433.
